precepts.text: Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments. I thought he kicked them out of heaven for disobedience? They do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word. Ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure: keep that word ministers in mind.
precepts.point: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
“Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” That do his commandments. I thought he kicked them out of heaven because they were disobedient and tried to overthrow him, and now they are fallen? No: they do his commandments. We just read about the spirit sent forth in 1 Kings 22, and about Satan working for the Most High in Job 1. The angels hearken unto the voice of the Most High.

“Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” Keep that word ministers in mind. They minister unto the Most High, doing his pleasure, and they also minister unto us.

“Bless the Lord, all his works in all places of his dominion: bless the Lord, O my soul.” Every angel in every place of his dominion is under his rule, carrying out his commandments, which is why Satan could only go as far as the Lord allowed him with Job.

precepts.text: As a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him. Isaiah 49:25, I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children. Zechariah 3:8-9, my servant the Branch, Christ, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. Revelation 12:10-11, they overcame the accuser by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony, and loved not their lives unto the death.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.” The Lord will have mercy and pity on those who fear him: not the unfaithful, but those who fear him. They are wisdom’s children.

Isaiah shows what that pity does: “for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.” The Lord will fight those who fought against us, and he will save our children, because wisdom exalts her children.

He does it through Christ: “behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH”, and “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.” That is what it pays to be faithful and diligent: the Lord will pardon our iniquity and remove it.

And the end of it is in Revelation: “the accuser of our brethren is cast down”, and “they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.” We overcome by the blood of the Lamb; we must have faith and continue to be faithful, loving righteousness more than iniquity. The Father pities his children who fear him, and exalts them.

precepts.text: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction, who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies.
precepts.point: The inhabitant shall not say, I am sick; the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity. Psalms 103:1-4, bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits, who forgiveth all thine iniquities, who healeth all thy diseases, who redeemeth thy life from destruction.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
Isaiah ends, “And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.” Nobody is going to be saying they are sick. David shows why: “Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits”.

Watch the benefits: “Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies”. The same Lord who forgives all our iniquities heals all our diseases, and the Lord can redeem our life from destruction.

That is the hope amid destruction. While the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations and his fury upon all their armies, the people that dwell in Jerusalem are forgiven their iniquity and healed, never to say I am sick again.

precepts.text: Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of the word; doing his commandments is hearkening to that voice.
precepts.point: For the Lord thy God is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” Doing his commandments is hearkening to that voice.

Even the angels show it: to hearken unto the voice of the word is to do his commandments. So to be “obedient unto his voice” in the latter days is to keep his commandments; and “the Lord thy God is a merciful God”, he will not forsake thee, nor destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers.

precepts.text: His angels do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word; the voice of the Most High is his commandments.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God”. Now we do some precepting, word by word. What is the voice of the Lord? “Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” The angels hearken unto his voice by doing his commandments. The voice of the Most High is his commandments.

So to hearken unto his voice means to keep his commandments. Not hearkening to his voice is not keeping them, and that is what brings all these curses upon thee.

precepts.text: His angels that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word; obeying his voice is keeping his commandments.
precepts.point: What is his voice again? Precept upon precept: the voice of the Lord is his commandments, so cleave unto him by doing them, that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

note.label: Deuteronomy 30: Call the Curses to Mind and Choose Life

precepts.why:
“That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days”. What is his voice again? Precept upon precept: “Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” The angels hearken unto his voice by doing his commandments. The voice of the Lord is his commandments.

So obeying his voice is keeping his commandments, and you cleave unto him by doing them. He is thy life and the length of thy days, “that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.”

precepts.text: He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel; the righteous acts Samuel rehearses are those acts.
precepts.point: It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron and brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt. Now stand still, that Samuel may reason with them before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord which he did to them and to their fathers.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel.”

Samuel told the people, “It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt. Now therefore stand still, that I may reason with you before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord, which he did to you and to your fathers.” The righteous acts Samuel rehearses are those acts the Most High made known unto the children of Israel.

precepts.text: He hath not dealt with us after our sins, nor rewarded us according to our iniquities; as far as the east is from the west, so far hath He removed our transgressions from us. Even though believing in white Jesus, Allah, or Buddha or keeping your birthday was idolatry punishable by death, He is forever merciful to them that fear Him by keeping the commandments.
precepts.point: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord. The sacrifice of righteousness today is keeping the law and presenting your body a living sacrifice.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
We offer the sacrifices of righteousness and put our trust in the Lord, and this is why: “He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities. For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is his mercy toward them that fear him. As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.”

Believing in white Jesus, Allah or Buddha, or keeping your birthday, was idolatry punishable by death. Yet he has not rewarded us according to those iniquities. “Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.” He is for ever merciful to them that fear him, and fearing him is keeping the commandments: the sacrifice of righteousness.

precepts.text: He shows His word and statutes to Jacob and Israel; He has not dealt so with any other nation.
precepts.point: When Israel fled Egypt there were oppressed nations who came out with us; the Bible calls them strangers. But the ways of the Most High were made known to Moses and Israel.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel.” Look at that: his acts unto the children of Israel, not to every nation.

David says the same later: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.” He shows his word and his statutes to Jacob and Israel; he has not dealt so with any other nation, and the other nations have not known his judgments.

When Israel fled Egypt there were oppressed nations who came out with us; the Bible calls them strangers. But the ways of the Most High were made known to Moses and Israel, and no other nation was dealt with so.

precepts.text: He shall save His people from their sins, and His people are the Israelites.
precepts.point: As far as the east is from the west, so far He removes our transgressions; He pities them that fear Him, for He knows we are dust.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.” This is heavy because Christ came to forgive Israel of their sins.

The angel said of him: “And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” He shall save his people from their sins, and his people are the Israelites. The mercy and grace David speaks of, not dealt with after our sins, is Christ saving his people from their sins.

That mercy and grace is to Israel, and it is not so that we could continue in sin. As far as the east is from the west, so far he removes our transgressions from those that fear him.

precepts.text: To this agree the words of the prophets; David the prophet and Ezra the prophet say the same thing.
precepts.point: As far as the east is from the west, so far He removes our transgressions; He pities them that fear Him, for He knows we are dust.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.” David the prophet says it, and he is not alone: “And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written”.

To this agree the words of the prophets. David the prophet and Ezra the prophet say the same thing: the Most High has punished us less than our iniquities deserve. The prophets agree with one another, and the forgiveness of Israel's sins that David speaks of is what Christ came to do.

precepts.text: Ezra says the Most High punished us less than our iniquities deserve, agreeing with David.
precepts.point: As far as the east is from the west, so far He removes our transgressions; He pities them that fear Him, for He knows we are dust.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.” Ezra says the same in his prayer: “And after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this”.

The Most High punished us less than our iniquities deserve. Ezra the prophet agrees with David the prophet, and to this agree the words of the prophets. Israel's evil deeds and great trespass brought what came upon us, and still it was less than we deserved, and he gave deliverance.

That mercy and grace is to Israel, and it is not so that we could continue in sin. Christ came to forgive Israel of their sins, and this is the mercy David and Ezra both bless him for.

precepts.text: Through Christ is preached forgiveness, justifying believers from things the law of Moses could not.
precepts.point: As far as the east is from the west, so far He removes our transgressions; He pities them that fear Him, for He knows we are dust.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.” Paul preached what that mercy is: “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.”

Through Christ is preached the forgiveness of sins, justifying believers from things the law of Moses could not justify them from. Christ came to forgive Israel of their sins; that is the not dealing with us after our sins.

That mercy and grace is to Israel, and it is not so that we could continue in sin. As far as the east is from the west, so far he removes our transgressions, and he pities them that fear him.

precepts.text: We are commanded to teach our children the words of the Most High diligently.
precepts.point: The covenant is to such as keep His commandments and remember them to do them. To do them is an action word.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“But the mercy of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto children’s children”. His righteousness reaches children's children, and this is why we must teach our children in every generation, so they receive that same mercy.

The law commands it: “And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.” We are commanded to teach our children the words of the Most High diligently, in the house, by the way, lying down and rising up.

Man's days are as grass, but the mercy is from everlasting to everlasting on such as keep his covenant. The children must be taught the commandments so that they keep them and the mercy carries on to them.

precepts.text: The Most High is a God of knowledge, and by Him actions are weighed.
precepts.point: The covenant is to such as keep His commandments and remember them to do them. To do them is an action word.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
The mercy of the Lord is “To such as keep his covenant, and to those that remember his commandments to do them.” To do them is an action word.

Hannah says what the Most High weighs: “Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” The Most High is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. Not talk, actions.

So remembering the commandments is not enough; the mercy is to those that remember them to do them, and the doing is what he weighs.

precepts.text: Be doers of the word and not hearers only.
precepts.point: The covenant is to such as keep His commandments and remember them to do them. To do them is an action word.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
The mercy of the Lord is “To such as keep his covenant, and to those that remember his commandments to do them.” To do them is an action word.

James says the same: “But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” Be doers of the word and not hearers only. The man who only hears the commandments and does not do them is deceiving himself.

The covenant is to such as keep his commandments and remember them to do them. That is the doer of the word, and the mercy from everlasting to everlasting is on him.
